Detect and redact: YOLOX, PP-OCR and Rampart find faces, visual text and contextual PII before any request.

Act locally: Typed actions are grounded, gated, executed and verified on-device.

Privacy before AI access: Sensitive context is removed at the source—not after it reaches the cloud.
Minimum necessary context: Useful structure crosses the boundary; raw identity stays in a memory-only vault.
Two-sided safety: Context is protected outbound; actions are validated inbound.
Browser-native: The same privacy contract supports Chrome and Firefox builds.

Proven browser stack: WXT, TypeScript and Manifest V3 produce loadable Chrome and Firefox builds.
Local AI is practical: Quantized ONNX models run through ONNX Runtime Web; visual work is targeted to visible regions.
Server is replaceable: FastAPI speaks a strict schema and the planner uses an OpenAI-compatible endpoint for Qwen3-VL.
One-command operation: START.sh launches the model, API and judge site; STATUS.sh and VERIFY.sh expose failures early.
Current proof: Controlled privacy, action and fail-closed demos run end to end on the team laptop.

text:
Adoption path: Ship as a browser privacy layer that sits between existing users and cloud agent planners.
Deployment model: Free local extension + self-hosted/community server; managed enterprise policy and audit controls.
Cost control: Small on-device models reduce server-side vision load; only sanitized structured context is transmitted.
Scalability: Add domain adapters, policy packs and independently versioned models without changing the privacy contract.
Trust and retention: Visible redaction, confirmation gates and safe logs make delegated browser work understandable.

text:
Dynamic pages / stale targets: Re-observe after every action, bind actions to fingerprints and fail closed when state changes.
Cross-site variability: Use semantic DOM + ARIA first, OCR as fallback, then add measured domain adapters.
Resource pressure: Load models lazily, crop visual regions, quantize weights and keep a deterministic no-vision fallback.

Privacy & trust impact: Users can delegate browser work without sending their full screen, raw DOM or secret values to a planner.
Security & responsible automation: Local validation, confirmation and post-action verification constrain what server-generated commands can do.
Adoption & ecosystem impact: A reusable privacy boundary helps browsers, enterprises and public services adopt agentic assistance with visible safeguards.

For: Everyday pages containing identity, credentials or personal details.
Process: Read locally → detect → redact → send safe structure.
Benefit: The planner receives useful context without raw identity.

For: Tasks where a private value is genuinely required to complete the workflow.
Process: Bind a LOCAL_* handle → plan on the handle → resolve only at execution.
Benefit: Balances privacy with task completion; server never sees the secret.

Process: Typed action → local grounding → policy gate → verify or fail closed.
Benefit: Prevents stale, ambiguous or high-risk actions from silently executing.
